reason: Culturegraph EntityFacts URI for GND 118624822, which Wikidata already holds as a GND ID (and as the JudaicaLink ID itself).
German Wikisource author page 'Mark_Twain' is a Wikimedia sitelink of Q7245, not an external identifier; it is the same entity.
English Wikipedia article 'Mark_Twain' is the enwiki sitelink of Q7245.
ISNI 0000000121324854 is already one of the six ISNIs on Wikidata; only the URI form differs.
DBpedia resource Mark_Twain is derived from the enwiki article linked to Q7245; same entity, no Wikidata property needed.
German Wikipedia article 'Mark_Twain' is the dewiki sitelink of Q7245.
The article gives the death date as '2.4.1910' (1910-04-02), but Wikidata and every authority have 1910-04-21. This is almost certainly a typo for 21.4.1910.
'Florida, Missouri, Estados Unidos da América' is Wikidata's 'Florida' (Missouri) at a finer level of detail.
'Redding, Connecticut, Estados Unidos da América' is Wikidata's 'Redding' with state and country added.
'Innocents Abroad' is his 1869 travel book, the source of the article's Faial/Horta episode. Wikidata's partial work list lacks it, and it is a notable work.

The 'New York Tribune', 'Daily Alta California' and 'Philadelphia Press' are newspapers he wrote for (correct for Alta California and the Tribune). These are employer or affiliation facts, not family relations, so they do not conflict with Wikidata's family list.
'Florida (Mo.)' is the LC-style qualified form of Wikidata's 'Florida' (Missouri).
'Redding (Conn.)' is the LC-style qualified form of Wikidata's 'Redding'.
The MARC 368 group term 'Americanos' (Americans) corresponds to Wikidata's 'United States'.

These are 670 citations of his works and translations: 'Personal recollections of Joan of Arc', 'Prints i nishchiĭ' and 'Vasilopoulo kai zētianopoulo' (both The Prince and the Pauper), 'Przygody Huck'a' (Huckleberry Finn), a Japanese short-story collection and a Mongolian edition. Joan of Arc and The Prince and the Pauper are missing from Wikidata's partial list.
'Geviksman, V. A.' comes from a 670 source citation (a translator or editor of a Russian edition). He has no personal relation to Twain.
'Florida, Missouri, USA' is Wikidata's 'Florida' with state and country added.
'Redding, Connecticut, USA' is Wikidata's 'Redding' with state and country added.
IBDB's credit role 'Writer Source Material' (writer of the source material) matches Wikidata's 'writer'.
'Frank R. Stockton' and 'Jules Feiffer' are co-credited as source authors of the musical 'The Apple Tree'. The credit is shared, but neither has a personal relation to Twain.
The real-name heading's given names 'Samuel Langhorne' correspond to Wikidata's 'Samuel' plus the middle name, which Wikidata stores as family name 'Langhorne'.
'Φλόριντα της πολιτείας Μιζούρι' means 'Florida, state of Missouri', the same place as Wikidata's 'Florida', written in Greek.
'Συγγραφείς', 'Δημοσιογράφοι' and 'Τυπογράφοι' (writers, journalists, printers) are in Greek and match Wikidata's writer, journalist and printer.
'Αμερικανός' (American) corresponds to Wikidata's 'United States'.
'Samuel Langhorne' in the 'Clemens, Samuel Langhorne' heading is his real given name plus middle name, consistent with Wikidata's 'Samuel'.
The year-only '1835' from the 100 $d field matches 1835-11-30.
The year-only '1910' matches 1910-04-21.

'Twain, Mark, 1835-1910 (see also)' is the 500 link from the Clemens record to his own pseudonym identity. 'Rev. Lyman Beecher (descendants were correspondents)' is NUCMC collection context, not a relation, so neither conflicts with Wikidata's family list.

'Mark Twain V Veteran Famous memorial' has page badges glued onto the name, and the other values are family members' memorial names, not his name. Some of those relatives (Henry Clemens, Langdon Clemens, Pleasant Hannibal, Margaret and Benjamin Clemens) are absent from Wikidata's compared relative list.
'Florida, Monroe County, Missouri, USA' is Wikidata's 'Florida' with county, state and country added.
'Redding, Fairfield County, Connecticut, USA' is Wikidata's 'Redding' with county, state and country added.
'Florida, Missouri, United States of America' is Wikidata's 'Florida' with state and country added.
'Americans' corresponds to Wikidata's 'United States'.
'Living with sharks on the Georges River', 'Sydney Harbour: A Cultural Landscape', 'Tourism' and 'Americans' are titles of dictionary entries that mention him. They are not agents.
'Samuel Langhorne' is his real given name plus middle name, consistent with Wikidata's 'Samuel'.
'village of Florida (Missouri)' is the same place as Wikidata's 'Florida'.
'American' corresponds to Wikidata's 'United States'.
The year '1835' in the 200 heading matches 1835-11-30.
The year '1910' in the 200 heading matches 1910-04-21.
'statunitense' (Italian for 'of the United States', from the qualifier 'scrittore statunitense') equals 'United States'.
'Florida, Mo.' is Wikidata's 'Florida' (Missouri) in abbreviated form.
'Redding, Conn.' is Wikidata's 'Redding' in abbreviated form.

The GND identity links are all his own names: 'Clemens, Samuel Langhorne' (real name, 'Wirklicher Name') and the pseudonyms 'Snodgrass, Quintus Curtius', 'Conte, Louis de' and 'Bothwell, J. W.'. All of these are already in Wikidata's pseudonym and alias data.
The year-only '1835' in the heading matches 1835-11-30.
The year-only '1910' in the heading matches 1910-04-21.
The related names 'Clemens, Samuel Langhorne' (real name) and the pseudonyms 'Conte, Louis de' and 'Snodgrass, Quintus Curtius' are his own identities, already in Wikidata's pseudonyms and aliases.
DBpedia Mark_Twain is derived from the enwiki sitelink of Q7245; same entity.
Japanese DBpedia 'マーク・トウェイン' is derived from the jawiki article linked to Q7245 and matches the Japanese label.
NDL authority 00459304 is already on Wikidata as the NDL Authority ID; only the URI form differs.
The year '1835' from the WordNet gloss matches 1835-11-30.
The year '1910' from the WordNet gloss matches 1910-04-21.
'Florida (Missouri)' is Wikidata's 'Florida'.
'American' corresponds to Wikidata's 'United States'.
'원작 (original author)' is a film-credit role (author of the source work) and matches Wikidata's writer and novelist.
'허클베리 핀의 모험' is the Korean title of Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (here film adaptations), which matches a Wikidata work.
The year-only '1835' in the heading 'Twain, Mark (1835-1910)' matches 1835-11-30.
The year-only '1910' in the heading matches 1910-04-21.
'توين (مارك-)' is the inverted, encyclopedia-entry form (Twain (Mark-)) of the Arabic label 'مارك توين'.
'فلوريدا وهي قرية صغيرة في ولاية ميسوري' means 'Florida, a small village in the state of Missouri', the same place as Wikidata's 'Florida'.
The value '7b89c094-da28-4fdb-bcd2-ce0db0df923e' is a bare KulturNav UUID taken from a 'creator' link, not a work title. It is also not the person's KulturNav ID (3e04abfe-...).

'Charles Dudley Warner' is his genuine co-author of The Gilded Age (1873). That is a collaborator relation recorded on the work, not a family relation, so it does not conflict with Wikidata's family list.

'American Academy of Arts and Letters' is an organisation he belonged to (an early member, 1904). This is a membership fact, not a personal relation, and does not conflict with Wikidata's family list.
'Florida (Missouri)' is Wikidata's 'Florida'.

These come from VIAF-derived 950/955 co-author lists of illustrators and translators of Estonian and other editions: 'Kemble, Edward Windsor' and 'Williams, True W.' (illustrators), and translators such as 'Pravdin, Boriss', 'Toots, Villu', 'Tikerpäe, Elle', 'Sintenis, Franz' and 'Быстров, В.'. None has a personal relation to him.
The 'work' values 'Twain, Mark, 1835-1910' and 'Clemens, Samuel Langhorne, 1835-1910' are his own name headings, picked up from a reverse ^creator link. They are not work titles.
'Samuel Langhorn Clemens' is his real name with 'Langhorne' spelled without the final e, a spelling variant of Wikidata's 'Samuel Langhorne Clemens'.

'The Prince and the Pauper' and 'Приключения Тома Сойера и Гекльберри Финна' are TV adaptations of his works (the latter is the 1981 Soviet Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn series). The Prince and the Pauper is missing from Wikidata's partial work list.

These names come from source-data citations of editions: 'Bernard DeVoto' (editor), 'Thomas Hart Benton' (illustrator), and 'Stanislav Vinaver', 'Abdullah Karjagdiu', 'Milan Vujaklija' and 'Jelisaveta Marković' (translators). None has a personal relation to him.
